Chlamydia and gonorrhoea

Chlamydia is the most commonly diagnosed STI in England, and gonorrhoea is second, with 151,163 and 63,943 diagnoses in 2025. Most people with chlamydia have no symptoms. Both are treated with antibiotics. Learn about chlamydia and gonorrhoea symptoms.

HIV

HIV attacks the immune system and can cause no symptoms for years. Treatment is free on the NHS and highly effective. Learn about the symptoms and stages of HIV.

Syphilis

Syphilis often starts with a painless sore that’s easy to miss, and it can come back as a rash. It’s curable with antibiotics. Learn about the four stages of syphilis.

Not included: genital herpes and hepatitis B and C. To test for those too, choose the 7-in-1 STI test kit.

questions.question: Can you have an STI without knowing?
questions.answer: Yes. Most people with chlamydia have no symptoms. HIV can cause no symptoms for years, and the first sign of syphilis is often a painless sore that heals by itself. Testing is the only way to know, even if you feel well.

questions.question: Who is the Core 4 kit for?
questions.answer:
You don’t need symptoms to test. The Core 4 is a good choice if:

  • You’ve had sex without a condom, or with a new partner
  • You want a regular check-up for the most commonly tested STIs
  • You’ve had a full STI test before and want a lower-cost retest
  • A partner has told you they have chlamydia, gonorrhoea, HIV or syphilis
  • You’d prefer a private home test to a clinic visit

Not sure which kit you need? If you’d like to check for herpes and hepatitis too, the 7-in-1 STI test kit tests for 7 infections for £64.95.

Need help now? If you have symptoms or a partner has tested positive, contact a sexual health clinic now.

Possible HIV exposure in the last 72 hours? Contact a sexual health clinic or A&E as soon as possible and ask about PEP, medicine that can help prevent HIV after exposure. Don’t wait for a test result.

results.heading: How to read your Core 4 STI test results

groups.intro:
Every test has a C (control) line and a T (test) line. The C line shows the test worked. A T line, even a faint one, means something was detected. The chlamydia and gonorrhoea test has two windows, so you get a separate result for each.

TestWindow(s)NegativePositive
Chlamydia & gonorrhoeaCt (chlamydia) and Ng (gonorrhoea)C line only in bothC and T lines in the Ct and/or Ng window
HIVOneC line onlyC and T lines
SyphilisOneC line onlyC and T lines

Invalid: No C line in a window means that test hasn’t worked, even if a T line shows. Contact us and we’ll help.

notes.title: What if a result is positive?
notes.text:
Don’t panic. All 4 infections can be treated: chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis are cured with antibiotics, and HIV treatment is highly effective. Contact a sexual health clinic or your GP for a confirmation test and treatment. NHS sexual health services are free and confidential, and your recent partners may need testing too.

If you’ve had syphilis before, tell the clinic, because syphilis antibodies can stay after treatment.

notes.title: Good to know
notes.text: These tests are designed for screening and don’t replace advice from a doctor or nurse. For ages 16 and over.

questions.question: What does the Core 4 kit test for?
questions.answer: It tests for 4 infections: chlamydia, gonorrhoea, HIV (types 1 and 2) and syphilis. There are 3 tests in the box, and each gives its own result.

questions.question: How long do the results take?
questions.answer: Each test gives a result in around 15 minutes, read at home. There’s nothing to post to a lab.

questions.question: How accurate is the Core 4 kit?
questions.answer: When used correctly, each test is a reliable screening test. In clinical evaluations, 99.81% of syphilis results matched a lab test. Testing too soon after exposure can affect results, and any positive should be confirmed by a clinic or GP.

questions.question: Is a 4-in-1 STI test enough?
questions.answer: For many people, yes. These are the STIs most often checked together at sexual health clinics. But the Core 4 doesn’t test for genital herpes or hepatitis B and C. If you’d like those too, choose the 7-in-1 STI test kit.

questions.question: What’s the difference between the Core 4 and the 7-in-1?
questions.answer: The Core 4 tests for chlamydia, gonorrhoea, HIV and syphilis for £44.95. The 7-in-1 adds genital herpes, hepatitis B and hepatitis C for £64.95, so it’s £20 more for 3 extra infections.

questions.question: How much do I save with the Core 4?
questions.answer: The 3 tests cost £50.85 bought separately. The Core 4 is £44.95, so you save £5.90. The 2-kit Test + retest pack is £80.92, saving a further 10%.

questions.question: Can men and women use the Core 4 kit?
questions.answer: Yes. It’s for anyone aged 16 and over. The swab test works with a vaginal swab or a swab from the urethra (the tube you pee from).

questions.question: Does it test for throat or anal infections?
questions.answer: No. The chlamydia and gonorrhoea test uses a genital swab only. If you’ve had oral or anal sex, ask a sexual health clinic about throat or rectal testing.

questions.question: How soon after sex can I use the Core 4?
questions.answer: You can test straight away. If you test early and get negative results, retest chlamydia and gonorrhoea at 2 weeks, syphilis at 12 weeks and HIV at 90 days.

questions.question: What if one of my results is positive?
questions.answer: Contact a sexual health clinic or your GP for a confirmation test and treatment. Chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis are cured with antibiotics, and HIV treatment is highly effective. Your recent partners may need testing too.

questions.question: What does a negative result mean?
questions.answer: It means that infection wasn’t detected. If you tested soon after possible exposure, retest once its window period has passed. If you have symptoms, speak to a sexual health clinic.

questions.question: Can I use the kit while pregnant?
questions.answer: The swab test is not recommended if you are pregnant. If you’re pregnant and concerned about STIs, speak to your midwife, GP or a sexual health clinic first. HIV and syphilis testing is routinely offered during pregnancy through the NHS, and they can test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea safely.

questions.question: Which STI test should I get?
questions.answer: If you want a quick check of the STIs most often tested for, the Core 4 is a good choice. If you’d like the most complete check, including herpes and hepatitis, choose the 7-in-1. If you’re only worried about one infection, a single test may be enough. Read more about how STI testing works.

questions.question: What does a basic STI test check for?
questions.answer: A basic STI test usually checks for chlamydia and gonorrhoea, and often HIV and syphilis too. The Core 4 covers all 4 in one kit.

questions.question: Can you have chlamydia and gonorrhoea at the same time?
questions.answer: Yes. You can have one or both at once, and their symptoms look very alike. The Core 4 shows a separate result for each.

questions.question: How often should I take an STI test?
questions.answer: Test after sex without a condom or with a new partner, and regularly if you have more than one partner. A sexual health clinic can advise how often is right for you.

questions.question: Can I get a free STI test on the NHS?
questions.answer: Yes. NHS sexual health clinics offer free, confidential testing, and some areas offer free postal kits that you send to a lab. Many people choose a rapid home test for results in around 15 minutes, with no appointment.

questions.question: Will anyone know what I ordered?
questions.answer: No. Your kit arrives in plain, discreet packaging with nothing on the outside to reveal what’s inside. Your bank statement won’t show “Test Discreet” or the name of the test.

questions.question: How fast is delivery?
questions.answer: We ship within 1 working day, with discreet delivery across the UK.
